content:
- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to revert; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast 10–15 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment < 0.50 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to catch momentum shifts.
